response.markdown_report:
### Insights

**Starting point.** (1) Sampled training margins cannot establish validation ranking quality. Empty measurements require nulls and counts. (2) Feedback suggests specific recent interests matter, but does not establish an optimal recency weight. Transition associations cannot establish purpose, compatibility, redundancy, or ownership. (3) Architecture-aware hooks enable controlled interventions; position-aligned diagnostics must include any inference correction.

**Related work.** (1) Measuring Recency Bias [1] cautions against excessive recency emphasis. Perturbations measure reliance, not intent. (2) Petrov et al. [2] motivate history-aware pairwise controls, but transfer to these categories remains unverified. (3) Krichene–Rendle [3] distinguish sampled metrics from catalog ranking; Cawley–Talbot [4] explain validation-selection optimism. Neither training margins nor selected-winner bootstrap intervals establish generalization.

### Framework and directions

| Direction | Existing evidence | Proposed extension | Interpretation limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Temporal reliance | Sequence scores | Matched suffix/prefix deletion and shuffling | Length, positions, and implausible histories confound sensitivity |
| Transition structure | Training histories | Shrunk transition residual with popularity controls | Gains may reflect popularity suppression |
| Ranking reliability | Sampled margins | Paired validation hits, strata, and uncertainty | Conditional uncertainty excludes selection bias |

### Candidate ideas

Scores are originality/potential/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each assessment gives a positive and negative reason.

| Idea | Scores | Positive and negative assessment |
|---|---|---|
| Controlled temporal audit [1] | 4/7/3 | Originality: explicit controls, established ablations. Potential: reusable evidence, no direct improvement. Difficulty: small probe, positional confounding. |
| Controlled transition residual [2] | 4/6/5 | Originality: diagnostic integration, familiar ensemble. Potential: cheap complementary signal, popularity shortcuts. Difficulty: sparse counts, scoring parity and controls. |
| Popularity-stratified rank audit [3] | 3/7/3 | Originality: task-specific reporting, standard analysis. Potential: exposes uneven gains, cannot fix them. Difficulty: simple bins, small samples. |

### Selected idea: shrunk transition residual

At 0% progress, retain SASRec and test one reversible branch. The revised ratings reflect limited novelty and additional validation work. Define training-only adjacent counts C, row totals n, and smoothed training item popularity p. Crucially, r=(C−np)/(n+τ): absent pairs receive a popularity penalty. Improvement alone therefore cannot establish useful transitions.

```text
fix tau=20 as a heuristic; exclude padding from counts
p[j] = (training_frequency[j]+1)/(total_frequency+catalog_size)
r(i,j) = (C[i,j]-n[i]*p[j])/(n[i]+tau)
fit fixed neural-score SD and residual RMS on seeded training samples
score = neural/max(SD,epsilon) + alpha*r/max(RMS,epsilon)
select shared alpha in {0,.25,.5,.75,1}; prefer smaller alpha on ties
```

Retain unchanged SASRec. Exploratory controls independently tune popularity-only, exact penalty-only, count-only, and log-lift corrections on the same grid; compare last-item/history aggregation and marginal-preserving randomized edges before attributing gains to transitions. Report transition coverage and changes by source frequency, support, popularity, and history length.

Preserve routing, seeds, splits, trial artifacts, environment-based data access, and predictor-writer parity. Use sparse CSR counts, training-fixed normalization, explicit source IDs, and chunked catalog scoring. Preserve both diagnostic interfaces, restore model mode, and return definitions, counts, and nulls. Metadata summaries use only available titles/descriptions; simulator traits remain unobserved.

Select solely by pinned four-category macro validation HR@10. Save user hits; use 10,000 paired, category-stratified bootstrap replicates for descriptive intervals. Fixed candidates remain intact. Intervals exclude training/candidate variability and selection optimism. Twenty-user catalog summaries remain supplementary.

References: [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.09722), [2](https://research.atspotify.com/2026/10/do-sequential-recommendation-benchmarks-require-higher-order-sequence-modelling), [3](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/), [4](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html).

idea.description: Augment each category’s SASRec scores with a popularity-centered, shrunk last-item transition residual. Retain unchanged SASRec through zero correction weight and explicitly test whether improvements arise from transition information or popularity suppression.
idea.motivation: The supplied qualitative diagnosis suggests broad associations can dilute specific recent matches, but does not prove that greater recency emphasis helps. Transition counts provide an inexpensive complementary signal. Algebra exposes a shortcut: for unobserved pairs, the residual penalizes destination popularity in proportion to source support. Controlled comparisons are therefore necessary before attributing gains to specific transitions.
idea.implementation_notes:
Use only the prescribed training histories, retaining their existing chronological order. Count every adjacent nonpadding pair within each user's training history, including repeated transitions; never cross user or category boundaries. Let n_i=sum_j C[i,j]. Define destination popularity over all training interaction occurrences, p[j]=(f[j]+1)/(sum_k f[k]+M), for the M eligible nonpadding items. Fix tau=20 for this initial experiment as an explicit heuristic, not an established optimum. Set r(i,j)=(C[i,j]-n_i*p[j])/(n_i+tau); unseen source rows produce exactly zero correction.

Train the unchanged per-category SASRec with preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, and the environment's SASREC_EPOCHS default of 200. Obtain normalization statistics once per category from 10,000 training prefix–candidate pairs sampled with replacement using a separate seed-42 generator: sample uniformly from valid next-item training positions, use their causal prefixes truncated exactly as during training, and draw a uniform nonpadding candidate excluding the prefix and its next target. Skip positions without an eligible candidate and record the resulting count. Compute neural-score population standard deviation and residual root mean square in float64; clamp both at epsilon=1e-8 and serialize them. If the sample is empty, use scales of one and record the missing evidence. Do not normalize over evaluation candidates. Use s/sigma_s + alpha*r/RMS_r; dividing baseline scores by a positive category constant preserves its ordering at alpha=0.

Select a single shared alpha across all four categories from {0,0.25,0.5,0.75,1}, using only pinned macro validation HR@10. Break equal aggregate hit counts by choosing smaller alpha. Preserve the evaluator's tie handling and candidate sets. Save category scores and each user's binary hit for every configuration. Avoid independently selecting category weights: five choices per category would permit 625 combinations. Keep a cumulative configuration ledger across subsequent searches; small searches can still overfit validation.

For exploratory attribution, compare corrections -p[j], -log(p[j]), exact penalty -n_i*p[j]/(n_i+tau), count-only C[i,j]/(n_i+tau), and log-lift log((C[i,j]+tau*p[j])/((n_i+tau)*p[j])). Normalize each correction by its training-sample RMS and independently tune its strength on the same five-value grid. Unobserved log-lift pairs have a destination-independent correction; this avoids the residual's specific popularity penalty but can emphasize rare observed destinations. These controls are separate exploratory analyses, not free additional evidence for the primary selected model. Before claiming transition-specific gains, compare a randomized transition multigraph obtained through endpoint swaps that preserve source and destination totals; record seed, requested swaps, and accepted swaps. A history-aware extension averages corrections over the last five nonpadding items with normalized weights proportional to 0.5^age, age zero being newest. Treat this fixed extension as an additional exploratory configuration, not an established optimum. All computation and failed trials count against the shared budget; prioritize the primary branch and popularity controls before extensions.

Report target-pair support and candidate-pair support separately: for each validation user, target support indicates C[last,target]>0, and candidate support is the fraction of the fixed 100 candidates with positive counts. Report HR@10 changes by transition support, training source-frequency quartiles, target-popularity quartiles, and history-length quartiles, with category-specific bin boundaries derived only from training data, retained duplicate boundaries, and subgroup sizes. Do not treat these strata as additional selection objectives.

Store counts as sorted CSR rows; avoid an M-by-M dense matrix. Candidate scoring gathers sparse counts. Full-catalog scoring uses chunked neural matrix multiplication, initializes the analytic negative-popularity term, and adds sparse observed-edge corrections. Empty histories bypass potentially undefined all-padding neural features and return training popularity; a nonempty history with an unseen transition source receives the neural score alone. Apply the benchmark's existing seen-item exclusions without modifying evaluation.

Provide a shared scorer score(features, items, source_items) for inference and architecture-aware probes. Preserve predict_score(features, items) as the compatible neural-component scorer and explicitly identify its scope in metric definitions; probes measuring deployed scores must call the shared scorer with source IDs. At diagnostic position t, use sequence[:,t] as source for the causal feature predicting positive[:,t]. Mask padding targets and sources, handle B-by-L tensors explicitly, and never infer source IDs from cached features. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). view.model remains the actual trained nn.Module. Run under no_grad, restore the prior training mode in finally, and return metrics, metric_definitions, observation counts, and nulls for unavailable measurements. Distinguish scaled margins from rank-based evidence.

Keep controlled temporal interventions supplementary: remove matched newest/oldest counts, shuffle earlier items while retaining the last item, and shuffle the entire history using fixed repeated permutations and unchanged validation candidates. Report paired hit, target-rank, and score changes with explicit tie handling. Frequency-matched replacements can help assess popularity confounding. These are inference-reliance probes; they do not establish causal intent or retrained ablation performance.

For uncertainty, run 10,000 seed-42 paired bootstrap replicates, independently resampling validation users within each category while using identical indices for compared models and averaging the four category differences equally. Keep each user's candidate set intact. Label the observed difference and percentile interval exploratory: the interval is conditional on trained models and candidates and does not adjust for winner selection, training seeds, or negative-sampling variability. Do not create new splits or access held-out test outcomes during search.

Preserve DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], all four categories, dataset routing, single-GPU execution, and artifacts beneath the trial directory. Update the predictor writer to serialize/load CSR counts, popularity, tau, scales, correction type, shared alpha, routing, and fallback rules. Check loaded-versus-training scorer parity on fixed training histories and candidates, including sparse rows, empty histories, padding, and candidate batches. Available metadata consists only of public titles, descriptions, and timestamps; do not consume the generic input's unavailable ratings, reviews, categories, prices, or stores. For the twenty training users, catalog coverage, popularity, concentration, and evidence-qualified simulator judgments remain supplementary and cannot establish relevance or latent diversity/conformity. No benchmark gain has been measured.
idea.pseudocode:
for category in four_categories:
    fit unchanged SASRec using prescribed split, seeds, and epoch environment
    C = CSR adjacent-transition counts from nonpadding training histories
    n = row_sums(C)
    p = add_one_smoothed_training_occurrence_popularity()
    tau = 20
    residual(i,j) = (C[i,j] - n[i]*p[j]) / (n[i] + tau)
    training_pairs = sample_training_prefix_candidates(seed=42, count=10000)
    sigma_s = max(population_std(neural_scores(training_pairs)), 1e-8)
    rms_r = max(root_mean_square(residual_scores(training_pairs)), 1e-8)
    save counts, p, tau, scales, routing, fallback rules
for alpha in [0, .25, .5, .75, 1]:
    score(h,j) = neural(h,j)/sigma_s + alpha*residual(last_nonpadding(h),j)/rms_r
    empty_history_score(j) = p[j]
    obtain pinned validation hits without changing candidates or tie handling
    save every user's hit and category score
select shared alpha by four-category macro HR@10; prefer smaller alpha on ties
write predictor using the same scorer and serialized artifacts
verify scorer parity on fixed training-only examples
run prespecified supplementary controls, support strata, and temporal probes within budget
report paired stratified bootstrap interval as descriptive and selection-unadjusted
restore model mode after every diagnostic probe

originality.positive: Combines an architecture-aware diagnostic adapter with explicit decomposition of transition and popularity effects in a tightly controlled benchmark.
originality.negative: Transition counts, shrinkage, popularity corrections, additive ensembles, and their ablations are established methods; the contribution is primarily experimental integration.

future_potential.positive: An inexpensive, falsifiable test can determine whether local pairwise evidence adds value and motivate controlled history-aware extensions.
future_potential.negative: Sparse support, popularity shortcuts, and validation selection may explain apparent gains; the method cannot infer purpose, compatibility, or current demand.

code_difficulty.positive: The primary branch requires sparse counts and additive scoring without retraining a new architecture or fetching external resources.
code_difficulty.negative: Training-fixed calibration, efficient catalog scoring, diagnostic source alignment, reproducible controls, and predictor serialization substantially exceed the difficulty of the scoring formula alone.

related_work.title: Measuring Recency Bias (2024)
contributions: The supplied research summary describes a recency-bias diagnostic and evidence that excessive recent-item emphasis can hurt accuracy.
Motivates controlled temporal-reliance probes rather than assuming recency is beneficial.
limitations: Does not establish an optimal recency weight for the four target datasets.
Perturbation sensitivity alone cannot establish genuine user intent.

related_work.title: Do Sequential Recommendation Benchmarks Require Higher-Order Sequence Modelling? (Petrov et al., 2026)
contributions: The supplied summary reports strong history-aware pairwise baselines against reproduced SASRec/eSASRec models.
Motivates last-item and recency-weighted history controls alongside sequence encoders.
limitations: The reported Amazon categories differ from the target categories.
Does not directly validate the proposed residual, normalization, smoothing value, or ensemble.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled metrics can reverse model comparisons, including in expectation.
Supports distinguishing sampled training separation, pinned validation ranking, and catalog summaries.
limitations: Does not authorize changing the pinned RecHarness evaluator.
Does not establish full-catalog relevance from logged interactions.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains how optimizing a finite-sample selection criterion can overfit that criterion.
Supports limiting search flexibility and distinguishing descriptive winner intervals from independent evaluation.
limitations: Does not quantify selection optimism for this particular search without additional evidence.
Does not make a selected-winner bootstrap interval selection-adjusted.

related_work.title: NAIS: Neural Attentive Item Similarity Model for Recommendation
contributions: Provides a history-based item-similarity alternative with learned attention.
Motivates considering multiple history items when last-item transition coverage is sparse.
limitations: Does not establish gains for the proposed transition residual or these four categories.
A learned attentive model adds training and tuning costs beyond the minimal initial branch.

related_work.title: TALE: Temporal Linear Item Relationships
contributions: The supplied search results identify temporal linear item relationships as another pairwise control.
limitations: The repository reference alone does not establish matched benchmark performance.
Reproducing a separate baseline requires implementation and budget beyond the primary experiment.

related_work.title: Cross-validation: evaluating estimator performance
contributions: Provides background on model evaluation and uncertainty.
Supports distinguishing evaluation of fixed models from evaluation of a selection procedure.
limitations: The proposed category-stratified paired bootstrap is a task-specific protocol choice.
Fixed-candidate resampling does not capture candidate-generation or training variability.

related_work.title: scikit-learn: Common pitfalls and recommended practices
contributions: Documents the principle of fitting transformations on training data.
Supports saving training-derived score normalization rather than recomputing it on evaluation candidates.
limitations: Does not prescribe the proposed sampling procedure or score scales.
Training-only normalization prevents one leakage route but does not eliminate validation overfitting.

related_work.title: SciPy compressed sparse row matrix documentation
contributions: Documents CSR storage and efficient sparse row access for transition counts.
limitations: A storage format does not ensure efficient GPU integration or scoring parity.
Full-catalog inference still requires careful chunking and sparse correction application.
